tour.name: Ha Long Bay Private Day Cruise from Hanoi: Caves, Kayaking & a Seafood Lunch on Board
tour.subtitle: A private day on Ha Long Bay with a car from Hanoi and your own boat: the limestone islands of the 'descending dragon', Sung Sot cave, kayaking among the karsts or a bamboo boat at a floating village, Ti Top island's viewpoint and beach, and a seafood lunch on deck.

tour.overview:
Ha Long means 'descending dragon': according to legend, the gods sent a family of dragons to defend Vietnam from invaders, and the jewels they spat into the sea became the islands. Geologists explain the 1,600 limestone islands and islets as the result of millions of years of erosion of a drowned karst plateau. Many are hollow, full of caves and lagoons. Ha Long Bay has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994.

This private day takes you from Hanoi by car on the new expressway, about two and a half hours, to your own boat for the day. You cruise among the karsts, explore Sung Sot cave, kayak or take a bamboo boat into a hidden lagoon, climb Ti Top island for the view and swim, with a seafood lunch on board.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 12 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Hanoi
• Type: private car with driver and guide, private day boat with crew
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; steps in Sung Sot cave and about 400 steps up Ti Top

WHAT YOU SEE
• The limestone islands of Ha Long Bay.
• Sung Sot cave.
• Luon cave and its lagoon by kayak or bamboo boat.
• Ti Top island.
• Fighting cock rock and other famous islets.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private boat lets you choose quieter times at the caves and stay longer where you like; the expressway makes a day trip comfortable.

WHO IT SUITS
Travellers short on time, families and anyone who prefers a private boat to a shared cruise.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you have two days, an overnight cruise in Ha Long or the quieter Lan Ha Bay is magical. If you prefer rivers and rice fields, choose Ninh Binh.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Boats are suspended by the authorities during storms, mostly from June to October. The bay is often misty from January to March, which has its own beauty.

days.name: Ha Long Bay by private boat: Sung Sot cave, kayaking, Ti Top island and a seafood lunch
days.description:
What to expect: the limestone seascape of Ha Long Bay from your own boat, with a private guide, car, entrance fees, kayaks and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at 7:00 and drive east on the expressway, about two and a half hours, past rice fields and the industrial towns of the coast. At the international cruise port your private day boat is waiting, a wooden-decked junk-style boat with a sun deck and dining area. As you leave the harbour, the islands close in around you: Fighting Cock rock, two islets facing each other, the Incense Burner, and countless others covered in jungle, their bases undercut by the sea.

You land on Bo Hon island and climb to Sung Sot, the 'surprise cave', one of the largest in the bay. Its three huge chambers, lit with coloured lights, are filled with stalactites and stalagmites that guides name after animals and legends. Back on board, the crew serves lunch on deck: grilled prawns, squid, steamed fish, clams, spring rolls and fresh fruit.

In the afternoon you stop at Luon cave, a low arch in a karst wall that leads into a lagoon enclosed by cliffs. You paddle through by kayak, or are rowed in a bamboo boat by a local woman, and look up at monkeys in the trees. You end at Ti Top island, named after the Soviet cosmonaut Gherman Titov, who visited with Ho Chi Minh in 1962. About 400 steps lead to a viewpoint over the whole bay, and below is a small crescent beach for a swim. The boat returns to port in the late afternoon, and your driver takes you back to Hanoi, arriving at about 19:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:00 – Pick-up at your hotel in Hanoi.
09:30 – Board your private boat in Ha Long.
10:30 – Sung Sot cave.
12:00 – Seafood lunch on board.
13:30 – Luon cave by kayak or bamboo boat.
14:45 – Ti Top island: viewpoint and swim.
16:00 – Return to port.
19:30 – Back at your hotel in Hanoi.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Routes are set by the bay authorities; your captain chooses the best order on the day.
• Lan Ha Bay, quieter and reached from Cat Ba, can replace Ha Long on request.
• Boats cannot sail during storm warnings; we then rebook or refund.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, private guide, private boat, entrance and cave fees, kayaks or bamboo boat, lunch, fruit and water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks on board, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the boat really private?
faq.answer: Yes. You have your own day boat and crew; only your group is on board.

faq.question: How long is the drive from Hanoi?
faq.answer: About two and a half hours each way on the expressway, with a rest stop.

faq.question: Are entrance fees and lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes: the bay entrance, cave fees, kayaks or bamboo boat and a seafood lunch. Vegetarian menus are available.

faq.question: Can we stay overnight on the bay?
faq.answer: Yes, and it is wonderful. We can book a private or small boutique overnight cruise in Ha Long or Lan Ha Bay.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the caves, the kayaks and the beach. Life jackets in children's sizes are provided.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Sung Sot and Ti Top involve many steps; the cruise itself can be enjoyed from the deck.

faq.question: Can non-swimmers kayak?
faq.answer: Yes, with a life jacket; or choose the bamboo boat, rowed by a local.

faq.question: What happens in bad weather?
faq.answer: When the authorities suspend sailing for storms, we rebook your trip or refund it in full.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Vietnam but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes for steps, swimwear, a hat and sun cream, and a jacket in winter.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: March to May and September to November. Summer is hot with storms; winter is cool and often misty.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour, and at no cost if sailing is suspended. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
